messages:
maria: heads-up — after this morning's driver bump (cuda-driver 540) a subset of h100-prod started picking the short-sequence kernel for 512-token requests. p99 jumped ~22% on those hosts. :eyes:

 tj: saw the same in the canary. latency spikes correlated with KV-cache hitrate drops for chat workloads. autotune telemetry shows tie-breaker drift toward fastpath.

 anya: digging into selector logs — autotuner microbench scores for the longpath dropped slightly post-driver, which made the tie-break algorithm prefer shortpath for the 512 bucket. suspect kernel launch/occupancy differences with new driver.

 devon: quick numbers from perf telemetry this morning:
 - traffic-weighted p50: +3%
 - traffic-weighted p99: +22% (affected hosts)
 - cache.hitrate.prefix_longpath: 71% -> 6% after flip
 - kernel_selector.shortpath_rate[seq=512]: 8% -> 94%

 maria: here's the quick grep that shows the flip on one host (redacted):
```
$ sudo tail -n 200 /var/log/runtime/kernel-selector.log
[09:12:03] kernel_pick seq=512 model=redwood-3 longpath_score=0.42 shortpath_score=0.59 -> PICK=shortpath
[09:12:09] kernel_pick seq=512 model=redwood-3 longpath_score=0.40 shortpath_score=0.62 -> PICK=shortpath
[09:14:01] kernel_pick seq=128 model=redwood-3 longpath_score=0.10 shortpath_score=0.90 -> PICK=shortpath
```

 perf-bot: alert: autotune.hitrate_drop detected on h100-prod cluster h100-prod-az2 (scope=redwood-3, seq=512), severity=high.

 tj: immediate mitigation options we discussed: 1) rollback the driver on affected node pool to 535, 2) force-disable the shortpath tie-break (kernel_selector.force_longpath=true), or 3) hotpatch the autotuner to increase longpath weight for seq>=384.

 anya: my vote: 1 + 2 as a short window plan (fastest), then 3 for a safer mid-term fix while we re-bench with the new driver. I'll prepare the config flag change and smoke tests.

 devon: ops runbook (tested):
```
# rollback driver on k8s node pool 'h100-prod-pool-3' (example)
kubectl cordon node/<node>
ssh node/<node> sudo apt-get install --allow-downgrades nvidia-driver-535 -y
sudo systemctl restart runtime-agent
# after restart confirm selector version and kernel picks
ssh node/<node> sudo tail -n 50 /var/log/runtime/kernel-selector.log | grep seq=512
```

 ops-bot: initiated canary rollback on 5 nodes in h100-prod-pool-3 (run id: rollback-226543). Please monitor /dashboards/eng-runtime/autotune and the perf smoke job. :warning:

 maria: I'm running a 30m smoke across the canary nodes now. if p99 drops back toward baseline and cache.hitrate_longpath recovers, we roll to 20% then full.

 tj: addendum — get a heap profile/pc sample from one of affected containers (perf map) before reboot, we want traces for the kernel launch path differences.

 anya: noted. I'll attach perf samples and a small repro harness for the infra team once canary confirms. Also creating a short postmortem checklist: telemetry thresholds, autotune tie-break guardrails, and driver compatibility tests in CI.

 devon: long-term: add a deterministic prefer-longpath override for seq ranges used by chat; and build a kernel-selection simulation in our CI that runs after driver upgrades.

 maria: OK. next steps summarized: 1) continue canary rollback (ops-bot) 2) set kernel_selector.force_longpath=true on canary 3) collect perf samples 4) if green, expand rollback. I'll update this thread with smoke results. :thumbsup:
